web_events.query: US economic data release this week CPI GDP jobs
web_events.answer: This week, the most significant economic data release is the July Consumer Price Index (CPI) on Wednesday, August 12, at 8:30 a.m. ET. The CPI is expected to rise 3.4% year-over-year, slightly below June’s 3.5%. The July Producer Price Index (PPI) will follow on Thursday, August 13, at the same time, tracking price pressures further up the supply chain. Additionally, July’s jobs report showed a decline of 23,000 jobs against expectations of 80,000 gains, signaling a cooling labor market.

web_events.query: China PMI economic data this week
web_events.answer: China's PMI data for July indicated a slowdown in economic momentum. The official manufacturing PMI fell to 49.2 from 50.3 in June, entering contraction territory. The non-manufacturing PMI also dropped to 49.0 from 50.2, indicating contraction in services and construction sectors. The composite PMI declined to 48.8, reflecting a broader weakening in economic activity driven by soft domestic demand, the ongoing property sector downturn, and weather disruptions from typhoons.
